title: Metabolic Pathway Analysis by Liquid Chromatography Coupled to High Resolution Mass Spectrometry
author: Angelica S. Gouveia
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8vjhw4n
materials: High accuracy mass spectrum will be displayed .
Chong, J., Wishart, D.S. and Xia, J. (

steps.title: Sample Collection and Preparation
steps.instruction: Collect plant tissue samples and prepare them for extraction.

substeps.instruction: Immediately freeze samples in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
Macerate samples in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle without allowing them to thaw.
Weigh approximately 150mg of each sample into 2ml microtubes and record the weight for normalization.

steps.title: Metabolite Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract metabolites from the plant tissue.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl of extractive solution (80% methanol / 0.1% formic acid) to the microtubes.
Vortex for 20 seconds.
Centrifuge at 14,000 g for 20 min.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.22 µm PVDF membrane.
Transfer 80 μL of the filtered solution to a vial.

steps.title: NanoLC-MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform analysis using Nano Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (nanoLC/MS).

substeps.instruction: Inject a 10 μL aliquot using a nanoACQUITY UPLC system (Waters) with a trap column and a ProteCol GHQ303 C18 capillary column (3.0 μm – 300 μm × 150 mm) at a flow rate of 5.0 μL/min with a microESI ionization needle.
Use mobile phases: (A) water and 0.02% acetic acid (v/v) and (B) acetonitrile and 0.02% acetic acid (v/v).
Apply the following gradient program: 5% to 50% (B) over 30 min; 50% (B) for 5 min; 50% to 90% (B) over 3 min; 90% (B) for 2 min; 90% to 10% (B) over 3 min; steady at 10% (B) for 3 min.
Set ion scanning for MS1 spectra (positive or negative mode) between 100-1000 m/z and MS2 spectra between 50-1000 m/z.
Acquire data over 57.0 min per analysis using Hystar software (v3.2) and process spectra via DataAnalysis software (v4.0) in Auto-MSn mode.

steps.title: Data Conversion and Formatting
steps.instruction: Convert raw MS data to mzXML format for processing.

substeps.instruction: Install Proteowizard (32 or 64 bits).
Execute MSConvertGUI.exe to convert data to mzXML format.
Apply 'Peak Picking' filters for MS levels 1 and 2.
Rename spectrum files as ****.mzXML and group replicates into subdirectories by treatment.

steps.title: XCMS Online Processing
steps.instruction: Process the converted spectra using the XCMS online platform.

substeps.instruction: Create an account at https://xcmsonline.scripps.edu.
Upload .mzXML spectra for each treatment one at a time via Dataset > Add > Upload.
Rename the Dataset Name using an English abbreviation for the treatment and save.
Create a 'Pairwise' job: select the first treatment dataset, then the second.
Configure parameters: select HPLC/Q-TOF > Customized > View and Edit. Estimate m/z accuracy and maximum peak width for the system.
In the 'identification' module, select the metabolite library for the organism in study.
Save the method as 'myXCMS parameter' and submit the job.
Monitor progress in View Results and download the full results.

steps.title: Data Cleaning and Export
steps.instruction: Prepare the XCMS results for use in MetaboAnalyst.

substeps.instruction: Unzip 'result.rar' and open 'XCMS-diffreport-MultiClass.xlsx' in OpenOffice.
Delete column A and columns C through Z, retaining only column B (XIC area of detected/aligned ions).
Insert rows for 'name', 'sample', and 'label' to indicate treatments and replicates.
Save the file as a .csv (txt) file named 'XCMS-diffreport-MultiClass_yourprofile.csv'.

steps.title: MetaboAnalyst Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform statistical analysis and normalization using the MetaboAnalyst platform.

substeps.instruction: Go to https://www.metaboanalyst.ca/faces/ModuleView.xhtml, select Statistical Analysis > 'Peak Intensity Table' and format 'sample in columns (unpaired)'.
Upload 'XCMS-diffreport-MultiClass_yourprofile.csv' and use 'Standard Deviation' to remove low-quality results.
In 'Data Normalization', apply 'Normalization by median' and 'Pareto Scaling'.
Perform 'Cluster Analysis' (e.g., PCA, PSDLA, and heatmap) to identify treatment effects and metabolite variations.
Perform one-way ANOVA to identify dysregulated compounds (indicated by red filled circles).
Export results as TIF files at 600dpi, full page.

steps.title: MS/MS Spectrum Export
steps.instruction: Export high-resolution MS/MS spectra for identification.

substeps.instruction: Install and run DataAnalysis.exe.
Open the LC/MS spectrum file and apply a processing method (e.g., 'DataAnalysis micrOTOF Default_HUM_altaIntensidade100.m') to detect the 100 highest intensity ions.
Right-click 'TIC +all MSn' window and select 'find compounds Auto MSn'.
Set 'mass precision' to 4 in Display Parameters.
Select all compounds and chromatograms, then export as an .mgf file (e.g., 'myfilename.mgf').

steps.title: Metabolite Identification via NIST
steps.instruction: Identify putative metabolites using the NIST library search.

substeps.instruction: Install NIST and place the library directory in 'D:\NIST14\MSSEARCH\'.
Run 'nist ms search.exe'.
In 'library search options', select all libraries except 'mainlib', 'raplib', and 'nist_ri'.
Configure MS/MS for Q-TOF and low mass molecules.
Import the .mgf file and double-click the MS2 file to start the search.
Use 'Identity' and 'MS/MS' options with 'precursor ion m/z' set to 'in spectrum' and do not ignore the precursor for high-confidence matches. If this fails, try 'Similarity' 'simple' search.
